goal: Phase 3 (skill-registration) of campaign register-skill-and-harden: `faberun skills register` links the orchestrator skill into every installed harness that keeps skills, `faberun setup` offers it (and `--yes` does it, so install.sh registers on a fresh machine), the manual documents it, and README and GETTING-STARTED say what installing does to each harness. Spec: docs/campaigns/register-skill-and-harden/spec/SPEC.md.

taskPacket.objective: `faberun skills register [--harness a,b] [--copy] [--force] [--json]` discovers the skill directories of the installed harnesses and links (or copies) the faberun skill into each, and `faberun setup` offers and performs it.
instructions: Read docs/campaigns/register-skill-and-harden/spec/SPEC.md ('faberun skills register'), src/cli/skills.mjs (list/install, installSkills), src/cli/setup.mjs (the ask flow and --yes), src/host/home.mjs (faberunHome, installedVersionDir), src/cli/brand.mjs (renderUsage), src/seat/harnesses.mjs (the five operator harness names) and docs/COMMANDS.md (the section shape and the two-way command-surface test that enforces headings).

Discovery. A small table in src/cli/skills.mjs maps each harness to how its skills directory is found: claude -> `$HOME/.claude/skills`; codex -> `$HOME/.codex/skills`; the shared convention `$HOME/.agents/skills` (register there too when it exists, since some setups point the harness directories at it); zcode and agy -> measure on this machine: run `zcode --help` (it lists a `skills` command) and inspect `$HOME/.zcode` and `$HOME/.gemini` for a skills directory convention; register only where a real convention exists and record what you measured in a module comment; dsh -> no skill support (measured: its --help mentions none). A harness whose binary is absent is skipped with `[ok] <harness> · not installed`; one whose skills directory does not exist is reported `[warn] <harness> · no skills directory (<path>)` and skipped unless --force creates it.

Registration. The skill source is `join(faberunHome(env), "current", "skills", "faberun")` when the running CLI lives under the home layout (installedVersionDir(process.argv[1], home) is non-null), so a symlink follows every update; otherwise the checkout's skills/faberun resolved from import.meta.url. Default action: a symlink `<dir>/faberun -> <source>` (replace an existing symlink; refuse a real directory unless --force); `--copy` copies the skill tree instead (for a harness that does not follow symlinks). Lines: `[ok] claude · ~/.claude/skills/faberun · linked` / `copied` / `unchanged`; `--json` returns `[{harness, dir, action}]`. Register `register` in OPERATION_OPTIONS and usage.

Setup. After the config is written, `faberun setup` asks on a TTY `Register the faberun skill for <detected harnesses with a skills directory>? [Y/n]`, does it with `--yes`, skips it with `--no-skill`, and reports the same lines; `--json` includes `skills`. Reuse the register function; do not duplicate discovery.

Manual and references. docs/COMMANDS.md gains `### faberun skills register` (synopsis, flags table, what it writes, one example, the harness table with the measured conventions) and the new setup flag; skills/faberun/references/operations.md's 'Install, set up, update' section gains one line (ceiling 10917 in test/docs/docs-diet.test.mjs; trim or raise by the bytes added with a dated comment).

Tests. New test/cli/skills-register.test.mjs with HOME pointed at a temp directory containing `.claude/skills`, `.codex/skills` and `.agents/skills`: `skills register --json` links faberun into each (readlink resolves to this checkout's skills/faberun); a second run reports unchanged; a real directory in the way is refused without --force and replaced with it; `--copy` produces a real SKILL.md; a missing skills directory is a warn line, not an error; `--harness claude` limits the set. test/cli/setup.test.mjs: `--yes` with the same HOME registers and `--no-skill` does not. Every test spawns only bin/faberun.mjs.

Run tsc and `node --test test/cli/skills-register.test.mjs test/cli/setup.test.mjs test/cli/installer.test.mjs test/docs/` yourself and fix what they report. Never run npm install in the worktree; never run the whole suite yourself; never run tests that start and terminate child processes (test/run/, test/engine/seal-before-kill, unfreezable, supervise, judge, resume) -- your dsh sandbox cannot signal processes and they hang until the executor cap; the controller runs them as this node's verification.
decisions: Symlink by default to the installed current/ skill (follows updates), --copy for harnesses that need a real tree.
Discovery is measured per harness and recorded; dsh has no skill support.
setup offers it, --yes performs it, --no-skill skips it.
